BlackBerry Lifts Outlook on Automotive Software Revenue Demand — Interview
BlackBerry is expanding its automotive software footprint, defying broader sector headwinds, capitalizing on surging demand for high-performance computing into new models.

The momentum delivered a second-quarter earnings beat, prompting the company to raise its full-year forecast. Growth largely came from its QNX embedded software unit, which posted a 27% revenue surge, driving total revenue up 26% to $163.3 million, handily beating Wall Street forecasts.

"The market itself could be a little bit choppy because of the geopolitical and the macro type of things, but we are really well positioned," Chief Executive John Giamatteo said in an interview Thursday. "It's just a natural progression of technology: more software, more sophistication, more software domains are going into the car."

QNX is BlackBerry's operating system software that powers the computers in modern cars and commercial vehicles, and is increasingly expanding into non-automotive robotics and autonomous systems, such as medical tools and factory assembly.

Giamatteo said that QNX is capturing a larger share of the automotive market as carmakers rush to build software-defined vehicles, expanding the company's addressable market even as global assembly numbers stall.

He pointed to BlackBerry's recent design win this week with Coretura--which selected QNX's Alloy Kore middleware software for its commercial vehicle platform--as proof that the software is expanding beyond traditional automotive uses. "This was a great proof point right out of the gate," Giamatteo said.

BlackBerry, whose name was once synonymous with the early smartphone era, raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to a range of $616 million to $636 million, up from its previous projection of $594 million to $621 million. The company also boosted its adjusted earnings forecast to between 19 cents and 22 cents per share, compared with its earlier estimate of 16 cents to 20 cents.

QNX's better-than-expected revenue helped BlackBerry's total net income rise to $33.9 million, or 5 cents a share, from $13.3 million, or 2 cents a share, in the comparable quarter a year ago. Adjusted earnings of 7 cents a share topped analyst forecasts which were in line with company guidance calling for 4 cents a share.

QNX is expected to continue to support growth in the third quarter. BlackBerry said it expects the unit to contribute between $82 million and $88 million to revenue in the period, with total revenue expected at $143 million to $154 million. Secure Communication is expected to generate between $55 million to $60 million in revenue for the third quarter.
